title: stepwise-recovery-status-and-customer-postmortem-brief
public_summary: On 2029-11-20 at ~07:05 UTC we observed a regional streaming degradation affecting a subset of customer sessions in us-west-2. Our teams enacted rolling mitigations and routing fallbacks; service recovered to normal by 2029-11-20 09:40 UTC. This doc contains the status page wording and a concise postmortem for customers describing impact, cause, and actions taken.
status_page_update:
Initial: Investigating — We are seeing increased latency and truncated streaming responses for some requests in US-West (07:10 UTC). Engineering is investigating and routing some traffic to alternate regions.

Update (07:40 UTC): Mitigation in progress — Partial routing to alternative capacity reduced affected sessions by ~60%. Continued investigation into root cause.

Update (08:25 UTC): Recovery progressing — Autoscaling adjustments and cache reconciliation completed for primary region; errors continue intermittently for a small subset of long-running streaming sessions.

Resolved (09:40 UTC): Services returned to normal. We continue post-incident analysis and will publish a customer-facing summary with timeline, root cause, and recommended actions within 48 hours.
customer_postmortem_summary:
What happened: A rolling autoscaler change introduced during a capacity refresh caused a timing conflict between node termination and our streaming session cache reconciliation process. The conflict produced stale KV cache references for active streaming connections, which resulted in truncated or out-of-order streamed chunks for some long-lived sessions.

Why it affected customers: Sessions that spanned the autoscaling window and used continuous KV caching were most impacted; single-request calls and short-lived sessions were largely unaffected. Approximately 0.9% of streaming sessions in the region experienced degraded outputs or require session restart.

What we did: We immediately enabled regional rollback of the autoscaler change, applied an emergency cache reconciliation job to repair active session metadata, and diverted new streaming traffic to adjacent regions while the reconciliation completed. We also increased teams on-call and validated end-to-end streaming health with synthetic checks.

What we’ll do next: We are implementing stricter coordination between the autoscaler and cache lifecycle (safety handshake + leader election), adding an automatic session failover for streaming connections crossing a termination boundary, and expanding synthetic streaming checks to catch similar regressions earlier. We will also publish a longer technical writeup for customers with integration guidance in the coming week.
detailed_timeline:
07:05 UTC — Monitoring alerts: increased 95th percentile stream latency and several truncated chunk errors in us-west-2.
07:08 UTC — Incident declared; Customer Success and Eng SRE paged.
07:12 UTC — Initial mitigation: routing policy updated to prefer healthy hosts in adjacent AZ; error rate drops modestly.
07:30 UTC — Engineering identifies correlation with a rolling autoscaler deploy earlier in the window; cached session metadata shows inconsistent version tags.
07:40 UTC — Partial rollback of autoscaler change initiated to stop new host churn.
07:55 UTC — Emergency cache reconciliation prototype developed and validated on a small canary; applied to wider fleet.
08:20 UTC — Most affected sessions repaired; new sessions routed normally.
08:25 UTC — Continued intermittent truncation observed for a small set of long-running connections; manual session restart recommended for affected customers.
09:00 UTC — Fallback routing removed; system observes stable error rates.
09:40 UTC — Incident marked resolved; monitoring continues for 24 hours.
11:15 UTC — Internal post-incident sync scheduled; draft customer note prepared.
root_cause: A timing race between a rolling autoscaler change and the streaming session KV cache lifecycle produced cache metadata drift for active connections, causing stale references and truncated or misordered streamed payloads.
impact_and_scope:
Region: us-west-2.
Affected surface: streaming generation endpoints (long-lived connections with prefix/KV cache).
User impact: ~0.9% of streaming sessions returned truncated or out-of-order chunks; non-streaming APIs <0.05% error impact.
Customer profile: Primarily high-throughput customers using dedicated streaming sessions and long conversation histories.
mitigation_and_next_steps:
Immediate mitigations applied: rollback of autoscaler change, emergency cache reconciliation, temporary routing to adjacent regions.
Short term (next 7 days): enforce autoscaler-to-cache coordination protocol, add session-level failover to alternative host if termination detected, expand synthetic streaming probes to run every 2 minutes.
Medium term (30–90 days): implement a cache versioning guardrail in the runtime, add pre-termination session draining with graceful KV handoff, formalize runbook and automated remediation for cache drift events.
We will share ETA for each deliverable in a follow-up customer note and in product release notes.
customer_actionables:
If you operate long-running streaming sessions: 1) consider enabling cross-region routing for critical sessions while we rollout fixes, 2) restart any sessions showing truncated output (a new session will reconstruct KV state), 3) open a support ticket if you observe persistent duplication/truncation after 2029-11-25.
If you use Dedicated capacity: your account team will reach out with tailored mitigation history and any recommended configuration changes.
qa_snippets: Short: We experienced a regional streaming disruption that affected a small fraction of long-running sessions; service recovered after routing and cache repairs.

Long: A timing issue during autoscaler rolling changes caused session cache metadata to diverge for some active streaming connections, leading to truncated or re-ordered stream chunks. We rolled back the change, ran a reconciliation, and restored normal operations. We are adding automated guards to prevent recurrence.
For engineering contacts: see CONFLUENCE-INC-2029-11-streaming for full diagnostic logs and mitigation steps.
